Get ready for an intense live experience! Gurriers , formed during the pandemic, quickly made a name for themselves with their raw, mosh ready shows and sharp, socially conscious songwriting. After their critically acclaimed debut album, they return with their second album Nobody’s Coming To Save You , this time on a larger scale.

The new album, produced by Mark Bowen ( Idles ) and Loren Humphrey ( Geese , Cameron Winter ), takes the band’s signature sound to the next level. It combines driving rhythms, cutting guitars, and powerful vocals while remaining both refined and intense. Each track builds tension and grabs you by the throat, with lyrics that are honest, personal, and socially engaged.

Nobody’s Coming To Save You is about frustration, determination, and taking matters into your own hands. As the band themselves say: “If you look at it more deeply, it’s a call to action, no one is going to rise up if everyone expects someone else to do it. We all have to do our part in creating the change.” This conviction runs throughout the album, which is full of raw power, slow-burning intensity, and explosive passages, blending punk, post-hardcore, and more complex song structures.

Gurriers take the energy of a smoky underground club and transforms it into a stadium-sized experience.

A new Tommigun album . Ten years on from the last one: ‘Wooden Son’.

Coming home after all sorts of wanderings? Is that it? Coming home to that ugly, beautiful city, Brussels. Brussels is actually simple. The city moves you and then you want to lose yourself in it; or it doesn’t, and then you want to get away from it as quickly as possible. Brussels, Tommigun’s home town.

Songwriter Thomas Devos creates small, simple sketches of a few chords and a vocal melody in his music room in Molenbeek. He then takes these to Tommigun at Joeri’s garden shed on the outskirts of Brussels. The magic lies in the simplicity and the different personalities who bring it to life. Their heartbreak-hangover tunes are bittersweet songs with an underlying menace and the occasional searing outburst. A bit like Brussels. Raw and unpredictable, but with a great zest for life, despite everything. And with ‘Heavy Bones’, a fresh perspective has been opened up.

The album ‘Heavy Bones’ feels like a statement: ‘Heavy bones, heavy bones, I know… yes we head to the bones, head to the bones I know…’ We’re all on our way to the end, but not without throwing an intense party first.

Thomas Devos: Vocals, Guitar Kaat Arnaert: Vocals Pim De Wolf: Bass Joeri Cnapelinckx: Keys Bertel Schollaert: Saxophone Mattijs Vanderleen: Drums

No "bathroom floor", but a dance floor for Kids With Buns ! The Belgian indie pop duo is back with a new album and can't wait to perform it live!

Composed of Amber Piddington and Marie Van Uytvanck, Kids With Buns caused a sensation with their debut album “Out of Place,” concerts in legendary venues such as Ancienne Belgique, De Roma, De Vooruit, and OLT Rivierenhof, as well as a notable appearance on the VTM show “Liefde Voor Muziek.” The duo will release their highly anticipated second album this year. After both going through breakups, the duo started writing songs.

They moved to Philadelphia to collaborate with Jacob Blizard, former producer and guitarist for Lucy Dacus (member of Boygenius). There, they grew closer than ever, writing songs to support each other and recharge their batteries. Inspired by a chaotic period of sleepless nights and heartbreak, they created their most accomplished, profound, and ambitious work to date. Thanks to notable performances on the main stages of Belgian festivals, such as Pukkelpop, and concerts across Europe, Kids With Buns have built a solid live reputation. Their concerts offer sincere interpretations of vulnerable songs and intense experiences, touching every audience.

This concert is a co-production between Live Nation and Ancienne Belgique.

﻿ Impro’Nights is a concept by ALADAR that blends open mics and jam sessions. At the start of the evening, the audience is free to use the stage for a short performance in their chosen medium: music, dance, poetry, performance art, …

Then the jam begins; anyone can come on stage to sing, rap, dance, play an instrument, improvise…

ALADAR is a multidisciplinary artists’ collective, founded in Brussels by young artists from diverse backgrounds, cultures and artistic practices. They offer a lively, welcoming and authentic space where everyone can create, share and express themselves artistically without pressure, hierarchy or required qualifications.

In Brussels slang,

‘à la dar’ means ‘at home’:

and that is exactly what ALADAR aims to offer.

Since their formation in Plano, Texas, in 2010, Polyphia have made a name for themselves with a unique blend of technically sophisticated guitar riffs, hip-hop grooves, heavy trap beats and influences from progressive metal and rock. Since then, the band has released four studio albums: ‘Muse’ (2014), ‘Renaissance’ (2016), ‘New Levels New Devils’ (2018) and ‘Remember That You Will Die’ (2022). That latest album marked a breakthrough in popularity and influence, cementing their status as innovators and pioneers within the genre. Guitarists Tim Henson and Scott LePage, bassist Clay Gober and drummer Clay Aeschliman have played sold-out shows worldwide, racked up millions of streams and built a remarkably dedicated fanbase. With the release of the new single ‘Can You Feel It’, the arrival of a fifth album and the announcement of a tour in 2026, the band is all set for the next chapter.

This session will take place at GC Het Huys, Rue Egide Van Ophem 46, 1180 Uccle. Doors open at 7.30 pm and we’ll start singing at 8.00 pm. The session is scheduled to finish at 9.30 pm.

Do you want to improve your Dutch and do you enjoy singing? Then you’ve come to the right place! Every month, accompanied by two musicians and a set list full of Dutch-language classics, we head to a different community centre in Brussels. There, we practise Dutch together – through singing!

Super Concert and AB/Liveurope presents:

* The Black Wizards (PT) garage rock / proto-punk*

The Black Wizards are: Joana Brito(gtr/voc), José Gomes(bass/bv) and Helena Peixoto(drums/bv) Written as politics landscapes across the world spiral into disarray, the album channels frustration and urgency without sinking into hopelessness. While compiling lyrics, frontwoman Joana Brito drew inspiration from books on politics, gender and toxic masculinity, ideas that surface in songs taking aim at hollow leadership and social division. “Killing The Buzz” in particular cuts through political spectacle with sharp humour and punk energy.

Musically, Force Majeure & The Acts of God marks a decisive shift for the band. Moving beyond the sprawling haze of their earlier heavy psych sound, The Black Wizards lean into something leaner, rawer and more immediate. There’s garage rock swagger, wiry proto-punk tension and relentless rhythmic drive throughout, led by Brito’s jagged, commanding vocals, José Gomes’ gravelly replies and Helena Peixoto’s forceful drumming. Recorded in an intense five-day session with Cooper Crain in Porto, the album thrives on urgency, rough edges and volatile live energy.

De Kleine Boterhammen: Dutch-language afternoon concerts in an intimate setting

In 2026, our summer festival will be conspicuous by its absence, only to return stronger than ever in the summer of 2027. That’s why we’re launching De Kleine Boterhammen : a modest alternative that gives young, fresh Dutch-speaking talent every opportunity to shine in the meantime. All this with a view to progressing to the ‘De Grote Boterhammen’ at the renowned bandstand in the heart of Brussels Park.

From September 2026 to June 2027, on the last Thursday of every month, we’ll be organising a free afternoon concert in the newly renovated AB Salon. Everyone is welcome to come for lunch and enjoy some fine homegrown music at the same time. We will provide small sandwiches to nibble on, including the favourite sandwich of the artist performing that afternoon. You can look forward to seeing in autumn: singer/pianist FULCO ( De Beren Gieren , BeraadGeslagen ), the cynically cheerful bon vivant Frans Kalf , cabaret innovator Camilo Donoso and Mooneye frontman Michiel Libberecht , who is venturing into Dutch for the first time. Michiel Libberecht After eight years of focusing entirely on his Mooneye project and having played in just about every corner of the country – AB included, multiple times even – it was time for something new. Michiel Libberecht is now releasing music under his own name for the first time, and in his mother tongue too: West Flemish.

Girls In Hawaii is back with a new album and a European tour this autumn. To be released on September 25th 2026, the album Eldorado , marks a new chapter in a story that began at the dawn of the 21st century reconnecting resolutely with the alternative DNA of a band looking to the future.

With Eldorado , the band delivers their first studio album since Nocturne (2017). Formed in the early 2000s, Girls In Hawaii has established itself over the years as a staple of the European indie rock scene. With From Here To There (2003) to Everest (2013), via Plan Your Escape (2008), the band has built a musical universe that has left its mark on an entire generation. In 2023, they celebrated the twentieth anniversary of their debut album with a sold-out European tour.

In the press: “The Belgian revelation Girls In Hawaii has been redrawing the contours of pop since their debut album From Here To There. With a subtlety and intelligence that borders on insolence, Girls In Hawaii managed to establish in just one album what many Belgian bands struggle to find over an entire career.” (La Dernière Heure)

“From ideals to doubt, from fatalism to resignation, and from hope to fulfillment, it draws its coherence from this astonishing work in progress.” (Les Inrocks)

"Girls in Hawaii proves to be a gem of the post- dEUS generation." (3voor12 - VPRO)

A 50-year career calls for a big celebration! The legendary heavy metal band Accept is marking the occasion with its 50th Anniversary Tour 2026, an exceptional world tour that will stop off in Brussels. The German band will be performing at the AB on 13 December 2026 for what is already shaping up to be a legendary evening, with Dynazty and Enforcer, two support acts ready to set the venue alight!

Formed in 1976 in Solingen, Germany, Accept rose to the top of the international scene in the early 1980s, becoming one of the major forces in European heavy metal. With Wolf Hoffmann as its creative core, the band made music history with iconic albums such as ‘Breaker’, ‘Restless and Wild,’ ‘Balls to the Wall’ and ‘Metal Heart.’ Tracks such as ‘Starlight,’ ‘Fast As A Shark’ and ‘Princess Of The Dawn’ shaped the sound of European heavy metal and influenced generations of artists. Despite numerous line-up changes and several hiatuses over the decades, the band has been able to reinvent itself with force, particularly since the arrival of singer Mark Tornillo in 2009, releasing a string of critically acclaimed albums such as ‘Blood of the Nations’, “Stalingrad”, ‘Blind Rage’ and ‘Too Mean to Die’. As productive as ever, Accept returned in April 2024 with their latest studio album Humanoid, produced by Andy Sneap (Judas Priest, Amon Amarth, Testament, Saxon), another solid addition to an already impressive body of work.
5D95304C66CB5040913836C613D29DFB:
Trixie Whitley has been charting her own musical path for years now, balancing between past and future with an exceptional emotional intensity. Born in Ghent and raised between Belgium and New York, she was immersed in music from a young age: behind the drums at ten, a DJ by eleven, and touring Europe with theatre and dance companies as a teenager.

After a time as frontwoman of Daniel Lanois ’ Black Dub and a series of critically acclaimed solo releases, she has emerged as one of the most distinctive and groundbreaking artists of her generation. With Folded Time , the album that is to be released on Unday Records in late 2026, Whitley opens a new chapter: A nine track long journey through loss, reconciliation, motherhood and the slow work of healing.

The album came about between Brussels, Brooklyn and Montréal, with Whitley herself on drums, bass, guitar, piano and vocals. She was supported by the likes of Kid Koala , Stuart Bogie and Cem Misirlioglu . Without a rigid plan, entirely intuitively, she crafted an album that shifts from raw, tribal grooves to intimate, almost gospel-like reflection, always exploring the tension between transience and grounding, between trauma and joy.

Throughout it all, her voice is the beating heart: warm, open and fearless in touching both shadow and light. Folded Time confirms Whitley as an artist in full bloom, one who reclaims her story, her body, and her power and transforms it all into music that sparkles with life.

With mixed feelings, AB announces the farewell show of Channel Zero , as Belgium’s metal icons will call it quits in 2026. Formed in Brussels in 1990 around charismatic frontman Franky De Smet-Van Damme , the band has dominated the metal scene for decades with its impressive sound and energetic live performances.

From their breakthrough album Unsafe (1994) to their latest releases, Channel Zero has made a lasting mark on the Belgian and international metal scene. After taking a break in 1997, they returned in 2010 for a triumphant reunion, with six sold-out shows at AB. More hit albums followed, including Feed 'em With A Brick .

To celebrate their incredible career with all of the highs and lows, and their unbreakable bond with their fans, they will play their final show in the city where it all began. Join us at AB for an emotional farewell to Channel Zero.

Félicette is a project by Sam (Brorlab, Bontridders, Croptopcore).

Originally conceived as a way to experiment with turntablism and sound, the project gradually evolved into more traditional tracks with experimental folk elements. With “EP1”, Félicette created a bucolic landscape, featuring lush instrumentation and gentle tracks. Shortly after “EP1”, Sam was joined on stage by Mathilde Luijten (bass), Abel Ghekiere (guitar + clarinet) and Maurice Luijten (guitar). They toured Belgium and mainland Europe, with highlights including support slots for Caroline and Snuggle and performances at the Absolutely Free Festival and We Are Open.

Now they’re back with a full-length debut album, “Rope Cord Twine Thread String”, released on Toverberg, White Garden (Paris) and Mostly Interrupted. RCTTS builds on the gentle sound of EP1, but adds an ambitious production style that blends pop, folk and art rock. FFO: Broadcast, Feeble Little Horse, Stereolab.

From 2 is an indie folk mutant in the form of five voices, collecting the melodies and memories of those about to rock. They might sing each other’s memories as their own, or tell tall tales that feel very real. Either way, it will fit into a band.

They released their debut album on the Amsterdam-Paris label South of North, and played international support shows for bands such as Horsegirl.

Passi is one of the pioneers of French rap. Having first come to prominence with Ministère A.M.E.R. and then Secteur Ä, he has enjoyed a string of successes with his solo albums, including Les Tentations, a record-breaking gold disc, as well as with the collective Bisso Na Bisso. An artist, producer and entrepreneur, he has helped launch the careers of many talented artists and has left a lasting mark on the French-speaking music scene through his influence and longevity. This project celebrates a career spanning nearly 30 years by bringing together iconic figures and the new generation of French rap, confirming his role as a bridge between eras and his indispensable place in the musical landscape.

Having made their name with Rue Case Nègres and Le Bilan, they have sold over a million records. As artists, entrepreneurs and social activists, they are committed to passing on their legacy and will return in 2026 with a new album and an anniversary tour.
88A2D3CA3AB2DD472C289E53BC8AED72: SLIFT , a towering space-rock powerhouse and a relentless live juggernaut, announces a 2026 world tour, including one stop at AB. The French trio will be performing material from their upcoming album Fantasia , expected in June 2026 via Sub Pop . Every previous album by the radiant and heavy French trio—brothers Jean and Rémi Fossat and drummer Canek Flores, a friend since high school - has been a fantasia—a composite of genres and forms that allowed the band to improvise, to jam on themes until they seemed to spiral together into space. But, in a bit of intentional irony, SLIFT’s fourth album is called Fantasia without actually being one. It is, instead, their leanest and most direct record, a pointed saga about overcoming international upheaval delivered by a band bearing down without wasting a second. SLIFT didn’t want to lose the message by playing too much. They’re preparing for a battle they think we can still win.

What happens when we consciously slow down? When listening is more than a background activity and becomes a way to truly be present? Following previous, smaller editions in Pilar and AB, this year Resonate with expands into a two-day programme at the intersection of ambient, trance and sound healing. On Saturday at AB and Sunday at Pilar, we explore how sound can connect us with ourselves, with others and with the space around us. Especially for this two-dayer, we’ve invited NiXiE to curate. As DJ, music promoter and certified sound healing therapist, NiXiE has eclectic taste. She seeks out hidden gems and introduces you to experimental sounds and spiritual frequencies that tickle your senses.

Her programme invites you to let go of time for a while. Expect DJ sets, live performances, a workshop and a sound installation. During this intimate event at Pilar, you’ll experience music not only with your ears, but with your whole body. We’ll provide some softness to land on, so that you can listen while entirely relaxed, sitting or lying down. Feel free to bring an extra cushion or blanket for extra cosiness.

Resonate with is a collaboration between AB and Pilar, connecting artists who approach sound as more than just music: as a space for resonance, reflection, connection and new forms of consciousness.

Now presenting: the debut EP form Divee ! At this pre-release listening party we’ll listen to the EP in a cosy setting, followed by a short Q&A.

Divee grew up in Gaume, a small region in the South of Belgium. Raised in a rural environment, she is very inspired by nature, even though she might have spent more time head in the clouds than feet on the ground. Yes, she’s a dreamer and, as her dad would say : “dans la lune”.

Whether influenced by her mom’s love for alternative rock, her dad’s passion for classic rock and “chanson française” and her own discoveries of hip hop, r&b, soul, blues, pop and rap ; Divee’s inspirations are diverse and international.

She now brings her individuality to create a sexy, soft and bold sound. Gravitating around her love for r&b and hip hop, she uses her neo-soul voice to express sorrows and desires, to flirt with the audience or to touch on intimate subjects without shame. Her words are honest and authentic, tinted with poetry.

Fuelled by the voice that powered UB40 to 70 million record sales and over fifty UK chart hits, Ali Campbell is again bringing some much-needed reggae cheer into the world as he takes the latest incarnation of his extraordinary band to the world’s biggest stages. Building on a legacy that dates back 45 years to his formative years in inner-city Birmingham, singer and guitarist Ali’s touring ensemble remains the most authentic realisation of UB40’s original aim of advancing reggae in all its guises.

For Ali, who began a new era when he left the band’s original line-up in 2008, there’s no shortage of material to sing live. A typical show will include classic reggae covers such as Cherry Oh Baby, Please Don't Make Me Cry, Kingston Town and Red Red Wine – all from the hugely successful Labour Of Love series – plus more recent originals such as Unprecedented, from the 2021 album of the same name.

Music is often described as a universal language, but is the music sector truly accessible to all? How do neurodivergent people experience music, what challenges do they face at concerts and festivals, and how can technology, design and policy contribute to a more inclusive music experience? Inclusion is an important theme within the cultural sector, but accessibility is still too often viewed only in terms of physical mobility. Many invisible challenges still remain for those with a visual or hearing impairment and neurodivergent people. Think:

At the same time, more and more innovative solutions are emerging: vibrating floors, haptic technology, AI-driven live captions, audio-description and inclusive event designs. The question is not only what is technically possible, but also how the sector can embed inclusion structurally.

More information about the panel coming soon.

Her programme invites you to let go of time for a while. Expect DJ sets, live performances, a workshop and a sound installation. During this intimate event at AB, you’ll experience music not only with your ears, but with your whole body. We’ll provide some softness to land on, so that you can listen while entirely relaxed, sitting or lying down. Feel free to bring an extra cushion or blanket for extra cosiness.

Resonate with is a collaboration between AB and Pilar, connecting artists who approach sound as more than just music: as a space for resonance, reflection, connection and new forms of consciousness.

Blending French chanson with electric rock, Vernis Rouge weaves together the intimacy of the piano, the energy of the guitars and incisive lyrics. A Franco-Lebanese singer-songwriter, she draws inspiration from artists ranging from Barbara to Nirvana and No Doubt, creating a world where sensuality, boldness and romance converge.

She came to the attention of the wider public in 2024 with her unexpected cover of ‘Bande organisée’ on The Voice , and has since established her own distinctive style. Following ‘Comme des loups’ with Zaoui , she has collaborated on numerous tracks: ‘J’te laisserai pas partir’ with Mattyeux , one half of Vidéoclub, and then ‘L’Amour est une Garce’ with Jok’Air , released in September 2026.

Following a gig at La Cigale and with two upcoming shows at La Maroquinerie – the first of which is sold out – Vernis Rouge invites you to experience the full intensity of her world.

With mixed feelings, AB announces the farewell show of Channel Zero , as Belgium’s metal icons will call it quits in 2026. Formed in Brussels in 1990 around charismatic frontman Franky De Smet-Van Damme , the band has dominated the metal scene for decades with its impressive sound and energetic live performances.

From their breakthrough album Unsafe (1994) to their latest releases, Channel Zero has made a lasting mark on the Belgian and international metal scene. After taking a break in 1997, they returned in 2010 for a triumphant reunion, with six sold-out shows at AB. More hit albums followed, including Feed 'em With A Brick .

To celebrate their incredible career with all of the highs and lows, and their unbreakable bond with their fans, they will play their final show in the city where it all began. Join us at AB for an emotional farewell to Channel Zero.

This concert will take place at Super Fourchette, Zwaluwenstraat 3, 1000 Brussels. Super Fourchette is a 10-minute walk from AB, near Place De Brouckère. Tickets will be available at the Super Fourchette box office on the evening of the concert.

Unsafe Space Garden (PT) - unsafe jazz pop

Unsafe Space Garden are one of the most distinctive and compelling voices in the new wave of Portuguese music. Formed in 2019 in Guimarães, the collective has been building a unique artistic path where music, humor, and human connection coexist naturally. Their songs often emerge from sensitive or complex themes, yet they are transformed into something intimate, vivid, and full of light. There is awareness and critique, but also care, subtlety, and a clear desire to better understand the world and our place within it. Unsafe Space Garden are true chameleons, both on stage and in their repertoire, constantly reshaping their performance into something that deeply resonates with the audience. Their concerts move fluidly between intensity and intimacy, always leaving a lasting emotional imprint. Shifting seamlessly between English, Portuguese, and Spanish, USG demonstrate that when music is genuinely felt, language becomes secondary, and connection becomes universal.

In 2026, the band presents their new full-length record, O Melhor e o Pior da Música Biológica , their first album entirely sung in Portuguese.

Group Atelier is a feedback session for young artists. In a small group setting, we listen to work in progress, discuss artistic choices and explore the next steps together. These sessions focus on key stages in an artist’s journey.

During this Group Atelier, you’ll have the chance to receive feedback from Paulo on your demos, to help you refine your sound. This session will take place on 9 December, from 4 pm to 10 pm at the FRONTAL studio. Level: Emerging artists or musicians What to bring: Your own demos to share and receive feedback on Who it’s for: Emerging artists developing new material and looking for feedback Where: FRONTAL studio, Anspachlaan 77 When: 9 December from 4 pm to 10 pm

Paulo Rietjens is a Brussels-based producer and rapper, and co-founder of the rap collective Stikstof. As ‘Astrofisiks’, he has become a fixture on the Brussels scene. From his FRONTAL studio, directly opposite AB, he mixes tracks for artists such as Zwangere Guy, Charlotte Adigéry, Brihang, Victor De Roo, Le77, Selah Sue, UM!, Lander Gyselinck and Jazz Brak. What once began in a garage has evolved into a creative hub where he shapes artists’ sounds in collaboration with them. Paulo is known for his keen eye for sampling and attention to detail, and is thus actively contributing to the future of the Brussels sound.

Girls in Hawaii are back this autumn (with a new album and a major European tour). Their latest album, Eldorado, was released at the end of September and has opened a new chapter in a story that began at the start of the 21st century. The album is very much in keeping with the band’s alternative DNA, always looking to the future.

Formed in the early 2000s, Girls in Hawaii have established themselves over the years as a mainstay of the European indie rock scene. From From Here To There (2003) to Plan Your Escape (2008) and Everest (2013), the band have created a musical universe that has influenced an entire generation. Eldorado is their first studio album since Nocturne (2017). In 2023, they celebrated the 20th anniversary of their debut album with a sold-out European tour, the highlight of which was four (!) sold-out nights at the AB and a packed, brand-new KETCLUB*! The experience was so brilliant that the band wants to organise another KETCLUB to present their new album to the little ones. Yippee!

*KETCLUBs are proper concerts tailored for children. The AB offers ‘maskes’ and ‘ketjes’ (Brussels terms for girls and boys respectively) a genuine concert experience, similar to that of a traditional show for adults. The bands play a shorter set in the afternoon and we turn the volume down to 90 dB to protect children’s sensitive ears. A unique night out in a cosy setting. A friendly atmosphere guaranteed!

Blondshell , the project of Sabrina Teitelbaum , blends razor-sharp songwriting, dry humor, and crunchy guitars into gripping alternative rock. With her self-titled debut album in 2023, she broke through internationally: the record landed on none other than Barack Obama ’s Best Songs of 2023 list and immediately established her as one of the most acclaimed new artists of her generation.

Its follow-up, If You Asked For A Picture (2025), was also met with praise from outlets such as Billboard, Rolling Stone, and NME. Influences from Queens of the Stone Age and The Smashing Pumpkins run through a sound that feels raw, catchy, and emotionally brutal in equal measure. It’s no surprise that The New York Times dubbed her “an alt-rock supernova.”

Now, with more than 150 shows under her belt and collaborations with artists including Conor Oberst , Samia , Folk Bitch Trio , John Glacier , and Gigi Perez , she’s heading back on tour, including a stop at AB!

Their tracks have names like Pomelo Fog and their live performances shimmy from playful jungle to swampy techno and emotional line-dancehall.

Namer (fka Lazergazer) Namer is the latest moniker of Lazergazer, a Damascus-born DJ and visual artist now based in Amsterdam. NEK On weekdays, NEK creates shows blending theatre, dance and dramaturgy. Through DJing she continues her storytelling with the same freeform attitude. British-Sudanese singer Elmiene will perform for the first time at the AB as part of his first major international tour, Sounds For Someone Tour. Having made a name for himself with several heartfelt singles and impressive live performances, this Belgian stop will be the perfect opportunity to discover an artist whose talent and sensitivity are set to conquer the world.

Born in Frankfurt to Sudanese parents and raised in Oxford from childhood, Elmiene quickly established himself as a rising star of contemporary soul. From the outset, he has been praised by critics, accumulating nominations and awards (BBC Sound 24, Brit Awards 25, etc.), confirming his unique talent and solid artistic vision. His career, although still young, is distinguished by a sensitive and contemporary approach to soul, blending tradition and modernity, while offering a musical experience that is both intimate and collective. His debut album, “sounds for someone,” due out on March 27, explores true feelings and journeys between grief, acceptance, and love, blending universal intimate emotions. Produced by Sampha, Buddy Ross, NO ID, and Raphael Saadiq, the album includes the brilliant singles “Reclusive” and “Cry Against The Wind,” which have already racked up thousands of plays on streaming platforms, as well as magnificent collaborations with Baby Rose and Raphael Saadiq himself.

Kaat Van Stralen cannot be easily pigeonholed. What began as an original solo project grew into a genre-transcending punk band, complemented by Melvin Slabbinck (drums), Anton Robberechts (guitar) and Faust De Vogelaere (bass). Kaat herself takes care of the vocals.

Strict but fair, Kaat calls all genres to account. From punk and psychedelia to alternative spoken word. Expect heated linguistic noise, crackling beats, biting guitar riffs and pompous bass.

The impact did not go unnoticed. Humo called Stop Met Wenen “the most important Belgian song in ages”. De Standaard saw how the song went viral on TikTok, where young women lip-sync to the song while looking defiantly into the camera.

Kaat Van Stralen played more than 25 shows in the summer of 2025, with notable appearances at Pukkelpop, the Lokerse Feesten, Best Kept Secret, the Gentse Feesten and Crammerock, among others. At Pukkelpop, she played Stop Met Wenen with The Atomic Orchestra in addition to her own set. This autumn, Kaat Van Stralen will also conquer AB Club!
FA59BC120F6A0F66CC1496A6D0E240C7: Catharina Evens is an experimental electro-acoustic pianist who seeks to discover an alternative sonic palette for the acoustic piano. She does so by, amongst other things, manipulating acoustic sounds live using electronic equipment, amplifying them and having them resonate through the piano’s entire soundboard and strings. The typical acoustic piano sounds thus fades away, giving way to a distinctive world of sound – the many musical possibilities of which Evens further explores by way of improvisation and composition. The Belgian pianist creates her own absurd musical universe, full of narrative fragments, using granular textures, playful whimsy, compelling pianistic passages, naive phrases, percussive accents, piano preparations, rhythmic sequences and the exploration of the space between different musical genres.

On ‘Eternal Life No End’ (2026, Constellation Records), Radwan Ghazi Moumneh (Jerusalem In My Heart) and Frédéric D. Oberland (Oiseaux-Tempête) weave together Arabic vocals, bouzouki, saxophone and modular electronics into a mesmerising, often sombre musical form that balances between trance, improvisation and experimentation.

The music was created against a backdrop of war and upheaval in the SWANA region, and conveys feelings of grief, anger and perseverance without ever resorting to slogans or clichés. Throbbing rhythms, layered drones and melodies that seem to hover between memory and a hallucinatory dream state lend the compositions a unique intensity. The album has been hailed as a rare and successful fusion of traditional Arabic sounds and adventurous electronics, as compelling as it is elusive. Live, this music unfolds like a hypnotic ritual.

‘a fractured soundtrack to a conflict-torn world… delicate percussion is balanced by dense synth layers, wind instrument interludes, and post-rock walls of electrified bouzouki’ The Quietus
